historicalPreMain.scope: Two local CPU optimizations; preserves the pre-existing uncommitted working tree.
changes: Reuse the current route segment deck sample for vertical velocity and the extended walker row deck flag.
Evaluate the bridge/street-furniture signature only when its existing strict greater-than-one-second rebuild cooldown permits rebuilding.

walkerSync.method: Alternating original/current within one Node process; 30 warmup + 15 x 20 forced-rewrite syncs per version. Same state; complete Float32Array equality for 16/20-float rows and 4 speeds over 36 syncs.

equivalence.walkerRows: Complete Float32Array, dirty range and building event equality against the pre-change source: both 16- and 20-float row formats, speeds 0/0.5/1/8 over 36 updates on each workload.

props.method: City fixture: SHA256 of all geometry attributes, indices, instance transforms and visibility after each update; bridge style/progress/removal plus road/ground changes, strict cooldown boundary. At least three distinct geometry hashes required.

caveats: These are CPU sync microbenchmarks, not total frame-rate or GPU measurements.
Both sync versions run in alternating order within the same process with identical state; speed alternates 1/0.5 to force row rewrites.
The loaded city after 60 simulation ticks has only 54 moving walkers out of 2000. Its measured ~1% difference is too small to claim a practical improvement.

Dense workload assigns all 2000 walkers synthetic long segments, alternating a real city bridge and a 40-unit nearby ground route. Its gain illustrates the redundant sampling cost under heavy movement.
The props cooldown skips signature scans immediately after a rebuild; unchanged scenes beyond the cooldown retain their original scan frequency.
